recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-5456 unless Patient Care creates a new tracker for a broader redesign of Condition/Observation boundaries.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive DSTU1 Patient Care ballot comment #395 requested adding a Boundaries and Relationships section to the Condition resource that clearly distinguishes Condition from Observation.
initial_application: No git commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-5456 was found. The apparent application was 07aa93633f66b8d2d0b94692528feae41659d399, which added source/condition/condition-introduction.xml with a Boundaries and Relationships section and Observation-specific signs/symptoms guidance soon after the January 2015 ballot disposition.
additional_context: Condition is active in source/fhir.ini. Later Published Patient Care issues in the same source area, including FHIR-8872, FHIR-15970, FHIR-26904, and FHIR-38954, refined the Condition/Observation boundary and nearby scope wording; the current source reflects those later refinements. Current Observation narrative also points readers to the Condition boundaries section for clinical finding/disorder guidance.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was made because source/condition/condition-introduction.xml already has the requested heading and guidance explaining that signs and symptoms are typically Observation, while persistent symptoms requiring tracking or acting as proxies for an undetermined diagnosis/problem may be Condition.
